errors.name: Unauthorized
errors.doc: The caller is not permitted to perform this action.

errors.name: NotFound
errors.doc: The requested entity (escrow, proposal, subscription, ...) does not exist.

errors.name: InvalidInput
errors.doc: One or more arguments failed validation (e.g. zero amount, bad address).

errors.name: InsufficientFunds
errors.doc: The contract does not hold enough balance to satisfy the operation.

errors.name: AlreadyInitialized
errors.doc: The entity was already initialised; re-initialisation is rejected.

errors.name: NotInitialized
errors.doc: The entity was expected to be initialised but was not.

errors.name: DeadlineReached
errors.doc: An operation was attempted after its deadline elapsed.

errors.name: InsufficientAllowance
errors.doc: A required token allowance was lower than the amount being spent.

errors.name: Custom
errors.doc: Contract-specific error that does not map to the categories above.

errors.name: TokenTransferFailed
errors.doc: A SEP-41 token invocation failed (insufficient balance, missing or deauthorized trustline, undeployed token contract, or token-logic rejection). The raw token error discriminant is intentionally not forwarded — callers cannot tell which contract produced a forwarded code, so it is bucketed; the root cause remains visible in the transaction's diagnostic events.

errors.name: ContractInvocationFailed
errors.doc: A cross-contract invocation failed (target reverted or host abort). The target reverts are surfaced here so the caller can distinguish them from token-transfer failures, and the invoking transaction is left un-executed.

errors.name: WithdrawalLimitExceeded
errors.doc: The requested withdrawal would push a token's rolling-window total past its configured withdrawal limit. Kept distinct from [`ForgeError::InvalidInput`] so a caller can tell a policy rejection (a valid withdrawal that is too large right now) from a malformed argument.
